identity: An element is identified by the admitted constructor definition domain, node or edge definition name, ordered semantic key type descriptors and complete non-null typed key tuple. Node and edge definitions have distinct names in one domain. Reference key components use the identity selected by the existing admitted reference owner, not a mutable envelope or display name.
identity_domain: Issue from canonical constructor mapping and admitted producer-definition provenance. Exclude actual input Artifact CIDs, parameter values, Run or Invocation CIDs, graph content, row positions, storage locators, outer DATA aliases and source spans. Editing inline VALUES or mapping produces a different definition domain. Cross-domain comparisons require an explicit compatible mapping and otherwise fail.
content: Properties, label sets and edge endpoints are snapshot content, not element identity. Preserve element identity under content changes within the same admitted definition domain and typed key domain.
keys: Retain ordered composite key components without concatenation, display stringification or type coercion. NULL node and edge keys are excluded. Non-null duplicate node or edge keys in one definition are rejected even when payloads are identical. Check duplicate edge keys before endpoint exclusion.
endpoints: Resolve source and target typed key tuples against the declared node definition and key types. Exclude NULL or missing endpoints without synthesizing nodes. Independent edge keys retain parallel edges and self-loops.
labels: Node and edge label sets are separate from properties. Name lookup is case-insensitive while preserving admitted display spelling and property values. Each static label declares its exposed property subset; repeated labels require compatible complete property schemas. No data property implicitly creates a label.
admission: Use existing checked value and contract admission. Preserve full property contracts and nullability. Construct privately and publish no partial graph after duplicate, capacity or cancellation failure. Unimplemented operations reject explicitly rather than projecting to the legacy simple graph.
construction_bounds: Retain every ordered node-definition and edge-definition input occurrence, including repeated producer references. The node upper bound is the exact nonnegative safe-integer sum of node-definition input row bounds; the edge upper bound is the corresponding sum of edge-definition input row bounds. A missing definition family has bound zero; an unknown input bound is not zero. Total construction input rows sum both families before NULL-key or missing-endpoint exclusion. No endpoint-derived nodes are added. Reject overflow rather than rounding or saturating. These bounds are conditional on successful keyed admission, and do not discharge duplicate-key, value, completeness, authority, workspace, work, byte, cancellation or resource enforcement checks.
paths: Path values retain complete scoped node and independent edge identities. WALK permits reuse, TRAIL prohibits reuse of an edge identity, ACYCLIC prohibits reuse of a node identity. Preserve path multiplicity, including distinct parallel edges. Apply existing bounded traversal and retention owners.
snapshot: A separately identified 0.1 snapshot preserves the domain, full per-definition types, static label property subsets, element identities, endpoints and typed properties. Reload revalidates correspondence before handing off material. Snapshot content identity is distinct from element identity. Reject old-contract bytes and implicit conversions without changing the legacy snapshot contract or CIDs.
